items.stem: Out of the two – hydrochloric acid and acetic acid, which one is considered a strong acid and why? Write the name/molecular formula of one more strong acid.
items.answer: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is a stronger acid than acetic acid (CH₃COOH) because it releases H⁺ ions in aqueous solution more easily. In order to verify this, add a few drops of universal indicator solution to the test tubes containing the acids. It acquires red colour in hydrochloric acid (pH = 2) and yellow in acetic acid (pH = 4), which confirms that hydrochloric acid is the stronger acid.

items.stem: Write equations for: (i) Dissociation of HCl in water. (ii) Formation of hydronium ion. (iii) NaOH is dissolved in water. (iv) KOH is dissolved in water.
items.answer:
(i) HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻
(ii) H⁺ + H₂O → H₃O⁺
(iii) NaOH(s) ——H₂O——→ Na⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq)
(iv) KOH(s) ——H₂O——→ K⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq)

items.stem: What is dilution?
items.answer: Mixing an acid or a base with water results in a decrease in the concentration of ions (H₃O⁺/OH⁻) per unit volume. Such a process is called dilution and the acid or the base is said to be diluted.

items.stem: Tooth enamel is one of the hardest substances in our body. How does it undergo damage due to eating chocolates and sweets? How do tooth pastes prevent this damage?
items.answer: Tooth enamel is made up of calcium phosphate, the hardest substance in the body. When we eat chocolates, sweets etc., some particles remain in the mouth. The bacteria present in the mouth act on these left-over food particles to produce acid which corrodes the tooth enamel and causes tooth decay. As tooth pastes are generally basic, they help in neutralising this acid and prevent tooth decay.

items.stem: Name the gas which is usually produced when dil. sulphuric acid reacts with a metal. Illustrate it with an example. How will you test the evolution of this gas?
items.answer:
When dilute H₂SO₄ reacts with a metal, hydrogen gas is produced. For example, when H₂SO₄ reacts with aluminium metal, aluminium sulphate and hydrogen gas are produced.
2Al(s) + 3H₂SO₄(aq) → Al₂(SO₄)₃(s) + 3H₂(g)
When a burning match stick is taken near the mouth of the container in which hydrogen gas is being produced, it burns with a pop sound.

items.stem: A calcium compound which is a yellowish white powder is used as a disinfectant and also in textile industry. Name the compound. Which gas is released when this compound is left exposed to air?
items.answer:
(i) Bleaching powder or calcium oxychloride (CaOCl₂).
(ii) When exposed to air it releases Cl₂ gas, according to the following reaction with the CO₂ present in air:
CaOCl₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + Cl₂↑

items.stem: A metal compound A reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to produce a gas which extinguishes a burning candle. Identify the compound A and the gas produced. Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction if one of the compounds formed in the reaction is sodium sulphate.
items.answer:
Compound A is sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) and the gas evolved is CO₂.

(iv) A substance which dissociates on dissolving in water to produce hydroxide ions [OH⁻ ions]

items.stem: The soil in a field is highly acidic. List any two materials which can be added to this soil to reduce its acidity. Give the reason of your choice.
items.answer: To reduce the acidity, lime, magnesium oxide and magnesium carbonate are used. These neutralise the acid and thus reduce the acidity of the soil.

items.stem: P and Q are aqueous solutions of sodium chloride and sodium hydroxide respectively. Which of these will turn (i) Blue litmus to red or (ii) Red litmus to blue? Give justification for your answer.
items.answer: The solution Q will turn red litmus blue because it is a basic solution. No effect of solution P will be observed on either blue litmus or red litmus because it is a neutral solution.

items.stem: Name the acid produced in our stomach. What happens if there is an excess of acid in the stomach? How can it be cured? Name the antacid.
items.answer: Hydrochloric acid is produced by our stomach, which helps in the digestion of food. When we overeat, a large amount of acid is produced which causes a burning sensation in the stomach. Bases called antacids are used to nullify the acidity. Magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) is often used for this purpose.

items.stem: Explain why an aqueous solution of sodium sulphate is neutral while an aqueous solution of sodium carbonate is basic in nature.
items.answer:
(i) An aqueous solution of sodium sulphate is neutral because it is formed from a strong acid (H₂SO₄) and a strong base (NaOH).
(ii) An aqueous solution of sodium carbonate is basic in nature because it is formed from a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (H₂CO₃).

items.stem: Three solutions A, B and C have pH values of 6, 2 and 10 respectively. Which of the solutions is highly acidic? Which solution will turn red litmus blue?
items.answer: The solution with pH value 2, i.e. solution B, is highly acidic. The solution with pH value 10, i.e. solution C, will turn red litmus blue.

items.stem: How does the enamel of the teeth undergo damage due to the eating of chocolates and sweets? What should be done to prevent it?
items.answer: The best way to prevent tooth decay is to clean the mouth after eating food using a tooth paste, which is generally basic in nature and neutralises the excess acid formed in the mouth.

items.stem: A milkman adds a very small amount of baking soda in fresh milk. (a) Why does he shift the pH of fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline? (b) Why does this milk take a long time to set as curd?
items.answer:
(a) It is because he can keep the milk for a longer time, as milk in an alkaline condition does not get soured easily.
(b) Due to the addition of baking soda this milk becomes slightly basic, which neutralises the acids produced in the milk. Hence it takes a longer time to set as curd.

items.stem: A compound of sodium X is used in the kitchen to make the 'pakoras' crispy. It is also used to remove acid in the stomach. (a) Identify the compound X and write its chemical formula. (b) What chemical reaction occurs on heating it during the cooking of food?
items.answer:
(a) The compound X is sodium hydrogen carbonate. Its chemical formula is NaHCO₃.
(b) The following chemical reaction takes place while heating it during the cooking of food:
2NaHCO₃ ——Heat——→ Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂

items.stem: Write the chemical formula of bleaching powder. How is bleaching powder prepared? For what purpose is it used in drinking water?
items.answer:
The chemical formula of bleaching powder is CaOCl₂. Bleaching powder is produced by the action of chlorine on dry slaked lime [Ca(OH)₂].
Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O
Bleaching powder is used in drinking water to make it germ-free.

items.stem: Effervescence is formed when baking soda is heated. What substance is present in baking soda? Name the gas evolved. Write the chemical equation involved.
items.answer:
The substance present is baking soda (NaHCO₃). The gas evolved is CO₂.
2NaHCO₃ ——Heat——→ Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂

items.stem: What is 'baking powder'? How does it make the cake soft and spongy?
items.answer:
Baking powder is a mixture of baking soda (NaHCO₃) and an edible acid such as tartaric acid. Baking powder on heating produces carbon dioxide gas which causes the bread or cake to rise, making it soft and spongy.
NaHCO₃ + H⁺ (from tartaric acid) ——Heat——→ CO₂ + H₂O + sodium salt of tartaric acid

items.stem: Explain why plaster of paris should be stored in a moisture proof container.
items.answer: Plaster of paris should be stored in a moisture proof container because the presence of moisture can cause its slow setting by bringing about its hydration. This will make the plaster of paris useless after some time.

items.stem: What happens when a few drops of water are added to anhydrous copper sulphate? Explain with the help of an equation.
items.answer:
Anhydrous copper sulphate (CuSO₄) is white. When water is added to anhydrous copper sulphate, it gets hydrated and turns blue due to the formation of hydrated copper sulphate.
CuSO₄ + 5H₂O → CuSO₄·5H₂O

items.stem: State what happens when zinc granules are heated with sodium hydroxide solution. Write the balanced equation for this reaction. Name the main product formed in this reaction.
items.answer:
When zinc granules are heated with sodium hydroxide solution, sodium zincate salt and hydrogen gas are formed.
Zn(s) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂ZnO₂(s) + H₂(g)
The main product formed is sodium zincate.

items.stem: A substance X is used as a building material and is insoluble in water. When it reacts with dil. HCl it produces a gas which turns lime water milky. Predict the substance and write the chemical equation involved.
items.answer:
The substance X is CaCO₃, used as a building material and insoluble in water.
CaCO₃ + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g)

items.stem: Why is tartaric acid added into baking soda to get baking powder?
items.answer:
Tartaric acid is added to neutralise the sodium carbonate formed on heating by the decomposition of NaHCO₃. If it is not added, the cake would taste bitter due to the presence of sodium carbonate in it.
NaHCO₃ + H⁺ (from tartaric acid) ——Δ——→ CO₂ + H₂O + sodium salt of tartaric acid

items.stem: Explain why, while diluting an acid, the acid should be added to water and not water to the acid.
items.answer:
(i) When the concentrated acid is added to water, the heat is evolved gradually and is easily absorbed by the large amount of water.
(ii) If water is added to concentrated acid, a large amount of heat is evolved at once. This heat changes some of the water to steam explosively, which can splash the acid on our face or clothes and cause acid burns.

items.stem: What happens when an acid reacts with a metal oxide? Explain with the help of an example.
items.answer:
An acid reacts with a metal oxide to form salt and water. Example:
CuO(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CuCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l)
(CuO is copper(II) oxide, a metal oxide.)
The solution turns blue-green due to the formation of copper(II) chloride.

items.stem: What happens when a base reacts with a non-metal oxide? Explain with the help of an example.
items.answer:
A base reacts with a non-metal oxide to form salt and water. Example:
Ca(OH)₂(aq) + CO₂ → CaCO₃(s) + H₂O(l)
Here Ca(OH)₂ (calcium hydroxide) is the base and CO₂ is the non-metal oxide.

items.stem: Why do acids not show acidic behaviour in the absence of water?
items.answer: The acidic behaviour of acids is due to the presence of H⁺(aq) ions. Acids produce hydrogen ions only on dissolving in water. In the absence of water, acids do not produce hydrogen ions and hence do not show acidic behaviour.
